chapter_meta_description: Prince Xin invites his guests to present their children to an “immortal master” for apprenticeship. Han Li’s cold observation reveals the truth about this Qi Condensation fraud—and delivers a classic Mortal Stream lesson in social warfare.
og_title: A Mortal Journey: The Fake Immortal and the Sound Transmission
og_description: Han Li watches from the shadows as mortal nobles fight over a cultivator who’s barely above mortal himself. A chapter of cold amusement and a deadly quiet warning.
twitter_title: Han Li’s Cold Laughter: That “Immortal Master” is a Third-Rate Cultivator
twitter_description: Prince Xin throws a “meet your immortal master” party—but Han Li, from his seat, sees exactly how low the ladder goes. A study in power disparity and social tribulation.

lore_anchors.definition: A mortal honorific for any cultivator, regardless of actual cultivation level; even a low-level Qi Condensation practitioner is treated as a living god by ordinary people.
A basic cultivation technique that sends one’s voice directly to a specific listener’s ear without others hearing; used here by Han Li to deliver a private warning to Qin Yan.
A cultivator who has reached the second major realm; far above Qi Condensation and capable of crushing low-level “immortal masters” without effort.
A real-world Chinese web novel promotion event where reader votes count double for a limited time; the author’s note reflects the serialization culture of the genre.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn’t Han Li expose the fake immortal master?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because it is not in his contract—he is only hired to protect the Qin family from demonic cultivators, not to police every fraud in the mortal world. Exposing the old Daoist would draw unwanted attention to himself.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does Han Li’s “heh heh” mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a cold, contemptuous laugh that signals the “immortal master” is laughably weak. Han Li is implying that taking this man as a teacher would be a waste of the children’s potential—but the choice is still Qin Yan’s.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do mortal nobles get so excited over a low-level cultivator?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because the power gap between a cultivator and a mortal is absolute—even a Qi Condensation layer 5 or 6 practitioner can perform miracles like creating fire, healing incurable diseases, and living far longer than ordinary humans. To mortals, that is indistinguishable from a god.
